meta.description: A labeled Toggle Segmented Control with optional subtext and a small-avatar group below.

verdict.title: Fix — hasSubtext is still a variant axis
verdict.text: Rebuilt with a named Slot Container (three Avatars, shown by hasSlotContainer) and a Subtext Message. Still open: hasSubtext doubles the variants instead of being a boolean, and the header label is not a property.

traits.name: Reusable
traits.note: Four variants for what should be a single component with two optional slots. Any future trailing content (a count badge, an error message, a help link) requires a new variant.

traits.name: Self-contained
traits.note: Composes Toggle - Segmented Control + Subtext Message + Avatar instances. Inherits all 3 sub-components' open issues.

traits.name: Consistent
traits.note: Naming uses positional booleans (subtext=yes|no, avatars=yes|no) instead of slot semantics. Should be subtext?: String + avatars?: [Avatar].

traits.name: Composable
traits.note: Built from sub-components but doesn't expose them as slots — consumers can't swap the inner control for a 3-segment variant or use a custom subtext component.

open.headline: Boolean variant matrix instead of named slots.
open.body: subtext × avatars produces 4 variants for a slot-presence question. Replace with named optional slots — Figma Slot architecture supports this directly.

open.headline: Inherits all Toggle - Segmented Control issues.
open.body: No Pressed / Focused / Disabled state, hardcoded 2-segment count, positional first|second naming — all flagged on the parent component and propagate here.

open.headline: No way to change avatar count.
open.body: Avatar group is baked with exactly 3 avatars. Real consumers may want 1, 2, 5+. Should be a slot accepting avatars: [Avatar].

recommendations.headline: Convert boolean axes to named slots.
recommendations.body: Target API: EBSegmentedControlGroup(label, segments, selectedIndex, subtext?, avatars?). subtext and avatars become optional content slots driven by data, not variants. Drops Figma variant count from 4 to 1.

recommendations.headline: Adopt Figma Slot for both subtext and avatars.
recommendations.body: Use Figma's native Slot feature so consumers can instance-swap any Subtext Message variant or any Avatar group composition without detaching.

recommendations.headline: Promote inner control to a data-driven Segmented Control.
recommendations.body: Tracked on the Toggle - Segmented Control component — once that ships segments: [Segment], this group inherits the flexibility automatically.

recommendations.headline: Document the A11y model for the labeled group.
recommendations.body: Use aria-labelledby referencing the label. Subtext gets aria-describedby. Avatars below should be a separate accessible region with their own labels.

accessibility.ios: Use .accessibilityLabel on the segmented row referencing the header text, so the control is never announced as a bare "Label, Label".
accessibility.android: Wrap in Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = label } on the group container.

accessibility.ios: The segments are a single-select set — .accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected) on the active one, and announce position ("1 of 2").
accessibility.android: Use Modifier.selectableGroup() on the row and selected = true on the active segment.

accessibility.ios: The segment is 156 × 40pt. 40 is under the 44 × 44pt minimum — add 4pt of hit area above and below rather than resizing the control.
accessibility.android: Same geometry in dp; 40 is under the 48 × 48dp minimum, so extend the touch target without changing the drawn height.

accessibility.ios: Wire as .accessibilityHint on the segmented row so VoiceOver reads "Label, hint: Use this space for your subtext."
A separate accessibility region — the slot is arbitrary content and must carry its own labels, not inherit the group’s.
accessibility.android: Same. Give the slot its own contentDescription per child; do not merge it into the group semantics.

accessibility.ios: Header is 14pt and the segment labels 16pt — both must scale. The 40pt control height has to grow with them.
accessibility.android: Use sp for all three text layers and let the 40dp row expand with fontScale.

usageGuidelines.doText: Use the group when a segmented control needs a heading — it bundles FormGroup Header, Segmented Control and an optional Subtext Message at a fixed rhythm.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t reach for it to get a bare segmented control. With no header to show, use Segmented Control directly — the group always renders its 22px header row.

usageGuidelines.doText: Turn on hasSubtext for helper or validation copy under the control; it adds the 22px Subtext Message row and takes the component from 62 to 84.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t put validation copy in the header. The header is Primary/Label/Light/Small at full-strength #0A2757 and reads as a title, not a message.

usageGuidelines.doText: Use Slot Container for content that belongs to the selection — the recent-contact avatars it ships with are the reference case.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t leave hasSlotContainer off and expect the avatars to show. It defaults to False, so the slot and its three Avatars are invisible until a consumer opts in.

usageGuidelines.doText: Set the segment labels and the selected index in code.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t look for them in Figma. The nested Segmented Control is not exposed on the group, so segment count, labels and selection are all code-only — two segments is what the component draws.

scorecard.notes: Every part is a named instance — FormGroup Header, Segmented Control, Subtext Message — and the slot is a real SLOT node named Slot Container. The generic wrappers the 1.0.0 assessment flagged are gone.

Names follow the has prefix with lowercase values. But the two behave alike and are built differently: hasSubtext is a variant whose values are true/false, while hasSlotContainer is a boolean property. Both toggle one row’s presence; one doubles the variant count and the other does not.

The group owns no colour of its own — every value belongs to a nested component or to the slot’s example content, so there is nothing here to leave unbound. Bindings themselves cannot be read with the Talk To Figma plugin, so the Style tab’s token column is — rather than asserted.

A vertical container with a header, a control, and two optional rows — one a string, one an arbitrary slot. Maps to a single view on both platforms. The named-slot restructure the 1.0.0 assessment asked for has landed in Figma.

The group has no states of its own, which is correct — but the nested Segmented Control is not exposed, so nothing about selection, pressed or disabled can be reached through the group in Figma. Every consumer draws the same two segments with the first one selected.
No assets owned by this component. The Avatars inside Slot Container are example content and belong to the Avatar component.

variants.description: hasSubtext (2) = 2 variants. hasSlotContainer is a boolean property and Slot Container is a SLOT — both change what renders without adding a variant, which is why a component with four visible configurations ships only two. Heights below are with the slot hidden, as Figma ships it; turning it on adds 40.

changelog.header: Rebuilt in Figma on new node 26628:50778

rows.body: The component was rebuilt in Figma and never logged. The record still assessed 27:30940; the live set is 26628:50778. This entry is dated when the change was found, not when it was made — nothing in the file records the latter.
Figma Slots adopted. Slot Container is now a real SLOT node holding three 32px Avatars, replacing the baked-in avatar row. This applies the standing Adopt Figma Slot recommendation.

The boolean variant matrix collapsed. subtext × avatars produced four variants; the set now ships two — hasSubtext is the only variant axis, and hasSlotContainer is a boolean property that changes what renders without doubling the matrix.
Width corrected — 366 to 312. Every part of the component measures 312: header, control, subtext and slot alike.
Heights corrected. Documented as 64 / 86 / 104 / 118; read off Figma as 62 / 84 with the slot hidden and 102 / 124 with it shown. The parts are 22 + 40 + 22 + 40.

Gap is 0, not 8. The tab documented 8px between label, control and subtext. Every part is stacked flush — the rhythm you see is each nested instance’s own bottom padding, which means the group cannot tune its own spacing.

A Selected control was documented that Figma never had. The Style tab offered First / Second; the nested Segmented Control is listed under Nested instances and exposes nothing, so selection is code-only. The control is gone and Property Mapping now says so.
Style tab rebuilt to one card with the Figma property panel. hasSubtext and hasSlotContainer as toggles; Slot Container and the nested Segmented Control as static rows, since a slot takes no control.

Typography resolved to style names. Header Primary/Label/Light/Small, segment label Primary/Label/Base, subtext Secondary/Bold/Caption — all three matched. The tab previously wrote the header as a font spec, Proxima Soft Semibold · 16 / 16, at a size the layer does not use (it is 14 / 14).

Preview border radius fixed. The selected segment was drawn as a square rect clipped by a <clipPath>, the way Figma exports it — the clip did not resolve in injected markup, so the blue half rendered with square left corners. Redrawn as an explicit rounded path; verified in a browser.

Code tab rebuilt. Installation had no blocks at all and Usage Snippets and Usage Guidelines were empty. Property Mapping described the retired subtext=yes/no / avatars=yes/no axes, and the Variants Inventory listed four 27:309xx nodes at 366 wide.

Segment height is under the minimum touch target. The segment is 156 × 40 — below 44 × 44pt on iOS and 48 × 48dp on Android. The Accessibility table now says to extend the hit area rather than resize the control.

Two properties with the same job, built two ways. hasSubtext is a variant with true/false values while hasSlotContainer is a boolean property. Both toggle one row’s presence; only one doubles the variant count.

Nothing about the nested control is reachable. Segment count, labels, selection, pressed and disabled all live in Segmented Control, which the group does not expose — so every instance draws the same two segments with the first selected.
Token bindings unread. The Talk To Figma plugin returns no variable bindings, so all nine colour rows carry —. The previous record’s paths were not carried forward — they named the retired node.

meta.node still points at the retired 27:30940, and the Overview tab’s four open issues ask for changes this rebuild already made. Both are Overview scope and need a Component Review run — until then the Code tab and the Overview tab disagree.
Component assessed — 4 variants on subtext × avatars. Composes Toggle - Segmented Control + Subtext Message + Avatar. Documented
Verdict: Fix — Replace boolean axes with named optional slots (subtext?, avatars?). Drops variant count from 4 to 1 and unlocks any future trailing content. Open
C1 — Boolean axes — Slot-presence as variants. Convert to Figma Slot. Open
C5 — Inherited state gaps — Toggle - Segmented Control is missing Pressed / Focused / Disabled; this group inherits all of those. Open
C7 — Code Connect — Not registered. Blocked on slot restructure. Open
